lines.trans: Max, we need to talk seriously!
Hey, Vika! Glad to see you.
Oh, Kostya is calling, sorry!
Hello, Kostya, speak louder!
Hard to hear, I will come over right now!
Max, wait, do not leave!
Vika, this is a very urgent matter!
Kostya, why did you call?
What do you mean, I did not call you.
Pretend that you need help!
Oh, you are hiding from Vika?
Yes, play along with me, please!
All right, let us go to the storeroom.
Thank you, friend, you saved me!

meanings.note: only when answering or making a phone call

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind
иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind

examples.text: Из окна красивый вид на парк.
examples.trans: There is a nice view of the park from the window.

examples.text: Что вы имеете в виду, Клавдия Викторовна?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Klavdia Viktorovna?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
поставить громко = to put a phone on speaker

examples.text: Не говорите так громко, дети спят.
examples.trans: Don't speak so loudly, the children are asleep.

examples.text: Ой, это Илона! Я громко поставлю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's Ilona! I'll put it on speaker.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

examples.text: Бывший мой попросил, чтобы я подыграла ему.
examples.trans: My ex asked me to play along for him.

examples.text: Просто бывший мой попросил, чтобы я подыграла ему.
examples.trans: My ex simply asked me to play along for him.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to hide oneself, to be in hiding
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hide (oneself)', paired with 'спрятаться'.

examples.trans: Children love hiding in the wardrobe.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: У нас с тобой серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: You and I have a serious talk to have.

examples.text: Есть интересный разговор. Всё хорошо, малыш.
examples.trans: There's an interesting conversation. Everything is fine, kid.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку. Он меня ждёт.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man. He is waiting for me.

examples.text: Это старый заброшенный склад за городом.
examples.trans: It is an old abandoned warehouse outside town.

examples.text: Хорошо, тогда встретимся на этом складе.
examples.trans: Fine, then we will meet at this warehouse.

examples.text: Ищи на складе и быстрее крутись!
examples.trans: Search in the storage and hustle faster!
You can barely hear anything here.

examples.text: Товарищ майор, тут всё очень плохо слышно. Качества всё равно не будет.
examples.trans: Comrade Major, you can barely hear anything here. There won't be any quality anyway.
What do you mean? Where is Mishkin?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пастись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to escape, to be saved', paired with 'спасаться'.

examples.trans: I escaped from a serious conversation!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent, pressing').

examples.trans: This is a very urgent matter.

examples.text: Яков Григорьевич, у меня срочный вопрос к вам.
examples.trans: Yakov Grigoryevich, I have an urgent question for you.
